title: Dyadic denominator law for the phase constants of the Jacobi zeros
statement:
Let $\kappa_r(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}[A,B]$ be the $r$-th additive phase constant in the asymptotic phase equation for the zeros of Jacobi polynomials, with $A=\alpha^2$ and $B= eta^2$. If $\operatorname{den}(\kappa_r)$ denotes the least positive integer clearing the denominators of all coefficients of $\kappa_r$, prove that, for every integer $r\geq 1$, $
u_2(\operatorname{den}(\kappa_r))=E_r$, where $E_r=3r-1+
u_2((r-1)!)$. Equivalently, $2^{E_r}\kappa_r\in\mathbb{Z}_2[A,B]$, while $2^{E_r-1}\kappa_r
otin\mathbb{Z}_2[A,B]$. The established odd-part bound is that the odd part of $\operatorname{den}(\kappa_r)$ divides $\operatorname{lcm}(1,3,\ldots,2r-1)$; the sharp conjecture concerns the exact dyadic exponent.
references: - [The dyadic denominator law for the phase constants of the Jacobi zeros](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23006) — arXiv

progress.label: Open · progress reported
progress.tldr: A new paper makes substantial progress toward the denominator formula, but the proof of the sharp final law is not available in the retrieved record.
progress.summary:
The problem asserts an all-orders rule for the powers of $2$ appearing in denominators of phase constants associated with Jacobi-polynomial zeros. The retrieved material identifies neither the proposer nor the original date.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23006)*

**August 2026 structural reduction**

The paper proves divisibility and $2$-adic integrality bounds and reformulates the sharp law coefficientwise, supplying the structural reduction behind the claimed all-orders formula. The companion proof mentioned by the source was not retrieved, so this remains an unverified advance rather than a complete solution.



Current status (as of August 2026): Divisibility, $2$-adic bounds, and a coefficientwise reduction are claimed, while the sharp all-orders denominator law and its companion proof remain unverified.

*Caveats. The retrieved source reports the structural result but does not provide the companion proof needed to verify the final law.*

formulations.title: Coefficientwise $2$-adic formulation via the Legendre tangent
formulations.statement: Let $\Phi$ be the Borel transform of the Legendre tangent and define $W(t)=\sinh(2t)\operatorname{Im}\Phi(t)/t^2=\sum_{m\geq 0}w_mt^{2m}$. The dyadic denominator law is equivalent, with equality of the relevant valuations preserved index by index, to the coefficientwise condition $((2m)!)^2w_m\in\mathbb{Z}_2^\times$ for every integer $m\geq 0$.
